entries.title: Knowledge about the proportions having statin-dependent muscle symptoms (SDMS) to atorvastatin in a population with FH and self-perceived SAMS, as well as proportions with nocebo and misattributed muscle symptoms, can be used in the current patient follow-up to allow informative communication and potential improvement of the individual cholesterol-lowering treatment as well as improved follow-up of misattributed muscle symptoms. The use of treatment periods both with placebo and atorvastatin, as well as periods with no treatment, are essential to identify different mechanisms for muscular symptoms. Patients can use non-statin lipid-lowering treatment throughout the trial, and those who do not will be offered such treatment. The establishment of an objective biomarker that can distinguish between SDMS and nocebo/misattributed muscle symptoms would be highly valuable for assessment of muscular side effects and shared decision-making regarding the cholesterol-lowering treatment at the individual level.

header_row:
Participant must be ≥18 years of age at the time of signing the informed consent.
Participant having genetically verified diagnosis of HeFH or clinical diagnosis of FH with Dutch Lipid Clinic Network Score ≥9.
Participant with a history of self-perceived SAMS (i.e. muscle symptoms subjectively associated with statin treatment) on at least two different types of statins.
Participant having discontinued statin treatment due to associated muscle symptoms (must have been off statin treatment for at least 2 weeks prior to first assessment for study inclusion).
If woman of childbearing potential (defined as all premenopausal female that are not permanently sterile); participant must take a pregnancy test with negative result and express willingness to highly effective contraceptive use or adequate sexual abstinence during the study intervention (until the end of intervention).
Participant expected to be compliant with the requirements and restrictions listed in the informed consent form (ICF) and in this protocol.
Participant having access to a smartphone, tablet or personal computer throughout the study.
Participant capable of giving signed informed consent as described in Appendix 1.
